result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B is the better answer overall. Its colour cards show what each kept value replaces (for example, #0c3d5e and #0a3a5a are folded into #0B3C5D), it gives the totals (22 colours down to 12), and it has a jump nav to every section, so a developer can find things quickly. A's colour names describe roles (text, surface-page, border-strong), which is better than B's Navy/Blue/Sky, but its visible part doesn't say which values were merged. Neither screenshot reaches the components, so item 3 is scored conservatively for both, and item 4 also relies partly on the stated principles. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both screenshots show only the top of the page, so I couldn't see or fairly score the components or badge legibility in either answer. I gave the same estimated scores for items 3 and 4, but B states a status-never-colour-alone rule up front. Each swatch in A lists the hex codes it replaces, and A has a section nav with a 'Decisions to confirm' link, so merges are recorded and values are easy to find. B gives each color a clearer role name (surface-page, text-muted, brand) but says only in general terms that near-duplicates were merged. On balance A wins narrowly, mainly for showing what was merged.
